decision: Adopt ordinary structured finalization as an alternative at eligible pressure-checkpoint boundaries. No broad speedup or reliability claim.

implementation.eligibility: Structured finalization exactly true; context_headroom trigger; summary_checkpoint exactly true; continue/default continuation mode; outside active scoped subtask.
implementation.behavior: finish_attempt alone reuses normal parser, evidence resolution and terminal dispatch. Unfinished work uses the existing checkpoint_context path. One repair; no new time/token/call allowances. Frozen runtime packages remain unchanged.
implementation.audit: Distinguishes valid finalization not dispatched, incomplete dispatch and actual terminal handoff. Requires matching response/dispatch/payload and unverified terminal receipt; rejects later tools/inference or invented summary/reset.
implementation.observatory: Checkpoint acceptance is labeled unverified and awaiting dispatch. Separate user-reported list bug fixed: bound delegate review/application receipts replace perpetual awaiting-review labels in list and detail views.

findings: Both clean-task baselines saved a checkpoint explicitly stating review complete and only finalization remained; both reset and reread review.json. Both clean-task candidates finalized at the pressure boundary without a summary/reset.

Clean-task observed time pairs: baseline134.05s / candidate128.40s and baseline146.49s / candidate109.59s. All four had correct substantive no-actionable-findings conclusions and clean submissions, but candidate seed18310 overclaimed a scripted link/anchor check; full-result acceptance rejected. Candidate seed18311 has loose citation grouping of checks actually performed, retained as a qualification rather than a nonexistent-check claim.

Two candidate terminal handoffs were validated in actual frozen traces. Payload acceptance remains unverified model output, not semantic correctness; ordinary outer review still catches unsupported checking claims.

Unit controls preserve unfinished-summary/reset behavior, explicit review and scoped exclusions, one repair after malformed/mixed/truncated responses, supported blockers, original deadlines and resource caps, and interruptions between response acceptance and actual terminal dispatch.

Defective task: candidate99.80s and baseline101.20s both clean/structure-passing but unexposed to checkpoints. Both find the new-file write-rule conflict and miss the predeclared primary permanent-status/config write restriction. Both full results rejected; no timing attribution to checkpoint choice.

Qualification to the initial two-defect shorthand: the declared pair are primary issues, not an exhaustive inventory. The frozen defective packet and its sealed review also contain notebook-enablement and dependency-verification issues. Baseline raises the notebook issue (useful though phrased strongly as implied enum values); candidate does not. Neither finds the overbroad dependency-check claim. This does not change either rejection or the frozen plan.

No real-model unfinished-work checkpoint occurred in the six probes. Preservation of the summary/reset branch is supported by focused integration tests, not by an exposed unfinished-work trial in this batch.
qualifications: Existing known development tasks, six prospective probes only; not a reliability sweep. Every result retained and independently reviewed. Review structure checks are not semantic acceptance.

Paired snapshots, briefs, recipes, budgets and first request bodies match; the generated trajectories diverge before checkpoint exposure. Timing differences across full trials are not causal estimates of checkpoint savings.
Actual Delegate dispatch timings, not prefix-warmed ladder times. Generated finalization itself still costs time/tokens; its response uses the existing checkpoint2048-token/256-reasoning caps.
Scope remains narrow: no additional context recovery framework, new opt-in or automatic correctness certification. Explicit review paths keep their checkpoint/review semantics.
attribution: Local Worker authored the pure policy helper and its14 unittest methods, independently reviewed and verified then applied without repairs. Maintainer authored integration, audit, regression/UI tests, review judgments and documentation. Replay review artifacts were not applied to project source.
